The production of that feed and its distribution to various CDNs (a third-party provider, a major video platform, and it's own internal CDN), and then it's own internal CDN which is what distributes the feed to people using the service. My point is the first part is still used if you're using a third-party provider or something, you're only skipping the second part. So if the first part is the bottleneck (which doesn't seem to be the case here), using a third-party provider doesn't solve anything. Luckily, the second part seems to be the bottleneck.
